questions.q: What is the main purpose of a receipt reversal?
options: To change the currency of a receipt after the fact
To undo a recorded receipt because the money it represented didn't, or won't, actually arrive
To automatically create a customer statement
To merge two customers into one account
questions.explain: A receipt reversal undoes a receipt whose underlying funds failed to materialize, such as an NSF check or a data entry error.

questions.q: Which reversal method simply returns the applied transaction to its prior open balance, as if the receipt never happened?
options: Debit memo reversal
Standard reversal
Lockbox reversal
Automatic receipt reversal
questions.explain: A standard reversal is a clean undo: the receipt is removed and the transaction returns to its original open balance.

questions.q: Why is a debit memo reversal typically used for an NSF (bounced) check?
options: Because standard reversals are not technically possible in Receivables
Because the customer still owes the money, and a new transaction is needed to track that renewed obligation (often with a fee)
Because debit memo reversals are required for all receipts over $1,000
Because it automatically closes the customer's account
questions.explain: An NSF check means the customer still owes the amount, so a debit memo reversal creates a new open transaction to capture that, often along with a bank fee.

questions.q: With a debit memo reversal, what happens to the original invoice that the bounced receipt had closed?
options: It is deleted from the system entirely
It is reopened at its full original balance
It stays closed, while a new debit memo captures the renewed obligation
It is automatically written off
questions.explain: With a debit memo reversal, the original invoice remains closed; a separate new debit memo is created to represent what the customer still owes.

questions.q: Does Receivables retain a visible trail after a receipt is reversed?
options: No, the reversed receipt and any resulting debit memo are deleted
Yes, the original receipt, the reversal, and any resulting debit memo remain traceable
Only if the customer specifically requests it in writing
Only for reversals processed through lockbox
questions.explain: Receivables keeps the full chain of the original receipt, the reversal, and any resulting debit memo, supporting both audit needs and customer-facing explanations.
